model_identity_basis: requested command argument; actual resolved identity not exposed

defects: B-WHOLE foliage is organized predominantly into ascending, elongated fans rather than the overlapping lateral sprays and irregular interlocking masses visible in reference-0.
B-WHOLE lacks clearly hanging outer foliage comparable to the descending peripheral sprays in reference-0.
observations: The passes array follows comparison.required order exactly.
The overall crown outline and bare branching hierarchy support a match. Foliage organization prevents catalogue readiness in the leafy view.
Bark surface character remains unresolved at the supplied render scale; conspicuous repeated transverse markings warrant closer evidence.
anchor-0 establishes a stylized catalogue finish allowance, not permission to omit defining reference morphology.
These two views do not establish six-cell readiness or a seasonal transition.

findings.observation: Both candidate views show a substantial upright crown, broad lower-to-middle spread, narrowing rounded top, and fine projecting tips consistent with the reference outline range.

The bare candidate shows an upright framework dividing into ascending limbs, broad lateral branches, and repeated subdivision into finer twigs. Its crowded ascending interior remains compatible with the inventory's architectural description.

The leafy candidate has dark recesses and openings, but its dominant foliage units are long rising fans following the limbs. Neither the left reference's lateral shelves nor the right reference's irregular interlocking leafy masses is adequately represented.
Lower foliage reaches broadly outward, but peripheral sprays remain predominantly outward or upward pointing. The hanging outer foliage explicitly prioritized by the owner is not visibly established.

The rendered trunks are gray with repeated dark transverse bands. The reference close-up instead shows a largely continuous gray surface with subdued markings and irregular pale patches. The render scale does not reliably distinguish shallow coloration from pronounced surface relief, so the core bark-surface match and material readiness remain unknown.

Fine foliage grain and simplified rendering are compatible with the catalogue anchor's finish level. Leaf shape and detailed foliage material response cannot be established from the supplied whole-tree view.

The candidate base widens but ends in a relatively regular flat flare, whereas the photographed bases show irregular spreading ground contact. More irregular root flare would be a secondary refinement.
Differences in crown symmetry, exposed trunk division, and green intensity fit the variation visible across the photographs and do not independently block acceptance.

coverage.explanation: Broad lower-to-middle spread, upright proportions, a softly narrowing top, and fine peripheral tips match the photographed outline range.
Visible ascending structural limbs, outward laterals, and progressively finer ramification support the core architectural match.

Gray bark is supported, but repeated transverse markings cannot be reliably classified as shallow texture or prominent relief at this scale. The largely smooth reference surface is not sufficiently verified.
Dark recesses are present, but elongated ascending fans dominate over the reference's overlapping lateral sprays and irregular interlocking masses. This changes defining foliage organization.
Numerous fine elements support the coarse grain comparison, but their broadleaf character is unresolved. The inventory itself cautions that individual outlines are insufficiently visible.
The base widens, but its regular flat termination lacks the irregular spreading flare visible in the photographs. This is a secondary refinement.
Broad reach and an exposed lower trunk match, but clearly descending or hanging outer sprays are absent. Hanging foliage is an explicit owner priority.
Irregular pale patches cannot be confidently assessed on the narrow rendered trunk. Visible transverse bands do not establish a mottling match.
Lighter muted green exposed foliage and deep green recesses fit the photographed color variation.
A single exposed lower trunk dividing into multiple ascending limbs is compatible with the supplied framework variation.
Leafy and foliage-hidden views expose the relevant crown and framework evidence. This supports visibility-state coverage without implying a biological transition.
